To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the velocity distribution in the peripheral heavy-ion reactions contains a direct component centered near the beam velocity and an inelastic component at lower energies.

the velocity distributions for projectile-like fragments contain two components: (i) a direct component centered on the beam velocity and (ii) a dissipative component shifted towards lower velocities.
the experimental data for velocity distributions of projectile fragments in heavy ion reactions at Fermi energies are described well by the calculations in the transport model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
a new approach to the description of peripheral reactions with heavy ion.
a study of the asymmetry of the velocity distributions of projectile like fragments in the reactions of 22Ne (35 MeV) + Be and 18O(35 MeV) with Be and 181Ta targets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transport calculations reproduce the dissipative component well, while the direct component is underestimated by a factor of two.
transport calculations reproduce the dissipative component, but not the direct one, and the experimental data are in agreement neither with the direct component nor with the dissipative one.
the transport model calculations are in reasonable agreement with the experimental data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transport model describes well the velocity distributions of dissipative component, but it fails to describe the direct component.
the asymmetry of the velocity distributions in peripheral collisions is a sensitive probe of nuclear reaction dynamics.

the asymmetry of the velocity distributions of projectile fragments in the Fermi energy region can be explained by the transport calculations, and it is not necessary to introduce the additional effects, such as the momentum conservation, to explain this asymmetry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the asymmetry of the velocity distributions in peripheral heavy ion collisions is not a signature of a two-step process.
the transport approach provides a good description of the velocity distributions in the dissipative regime, but fails to describe the direct component.

the asymmetry of the velocity distributions of fragments in the Fermi energy region is determined mainly by the direct component, which is described well by a simple model, and the dissipative component, which is calculated by the Vlasov transport model.
